newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Sentrachem financial director quits.
newsitem.headline: Sentrachem financial director quits.

text.p: South African chemicals group Sentrachem Ltd said on Thursday that financial director Norman Kennelly was taking early retirement.

The company said Ian Collier, financial director of its NCP unit, had been transferred to head office and had assumed responsibility for the daily financial management of the group. A new group financial director is being recruited.

The move comes after a disastrous half-year for Sentrachem in which one-off charges of 261 million rand due to forward cover contracts and restructuring costs at its Sanachem unit, plunged the group into loss.
The company said it believed the problems at Sanachem had been adequately provided for and its results should show some improvement to the year end, with a return to profitability in 1998.
The group should see some improvement in the second half but financing and preference share costs would leave it with reduced attributable profit, before exceptionals, and a loss after exceptionals.
"Looking ahead to 1998, it is anticipated that profits will return to more normal levels, and the growth patterns of the group will be resumed," it added in a statement with half year results.
In the half year to February, Sentrachem took a 327 million rand exceptional charge before tax relief of 63 million.
Sanachem aside, Sentrachem said its other four main areas of operation remained sound, although fortunes varied.

Hampshire performed well with strong demand for its speciality products and dollar revenues up 20 percent on a year ago. Karbochem saw a doubling of operating profit, although some margin pressure is now being felt.

NCP was hit by very weak conditions in the flexible PVC market which uses its plasticisers and NCP year results are expected to be in line with the previous year. Safripol benefited from increased volumes and prices.
As part of the restructuring of Sanachem, sales were deliberately curtailed by more than 100 million rand in the first half.
